questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of a balanced XLR cable over an unbalanced jack cable?
options: Common-mode noise rejection through phase-inverted signal pairs
Higher maximum signal voltage across long cable runs
Lower cable capacitance, giving a brighter high-frequency response
Ability to carry phantom power on a two-conductor connection
questions.explanation: A balanced cable carries the audio signal on two conductors (hot and cold) that are 180° out of phase with each other, plus a shield. Any electromagnetic interference picked up along the cable affects both conductors equally (common-mode noise). At the destination (e.g., a mic preamp), the cold signal is inverted and summed with the hot signal — the audio adds constructively while the noise cancels. This is why balanced XLR connections are used for microphone and long-run studio cables.

questions.question: Describe the purpose of a DI (direct injection) box when recording an electric bass guitar, referring to impedance and signal level.
questions.sampleAnswer: A DI box converts the high-impedance, unbalanced output of an electric bass guitar into a low-impedance, balanced signal suitable for a microphone preamp input. Without a DI box, connecting a high-impedance instrument directly to a low-impedance mic input causes impedance mismatch, resulting in high-frequency loss and a weak signal. The DI box presents the correct load to the instrument (preserving tone) and outputs a balanced, mic-level signal via XLR, which rejects noise over long cable runs and allows the signal to be fed cleanly into the mixing desk or audio interface.
keyPoints: Converts high-impedance instrument output to low-impedance balanced signal
Prevents high-frequency loss caused by impedance mismatch
Outputs a balanced XLR (mic-level) signal for the preamp
Ground lift switch eliminates ground loop hum
Allows long cable runs without noise pickup
questions.explanation: Impedance matching is critical: a passive instrument like a bass guitar has a high output impedance (typically 10–30 kΩ). A mic preamp expects a low-impedance source (150–600 Ω). Mismatching loads the source, rolls off high frequencies, and reduces signal level. The DI box's active or passive transformer circuit bridges this difference. Many DI boxes also include a ground lift switch to break ground loops that cause mains hum.

questions.question: Explain the signal flow from a microphone to a recorded audio file in a digital recording setup, naming the key stages in order.
questions.sampleAnswer: Sound waves cause the microphone diaphragm to vibrate, generating a small analogue electrical signal (mic level, typically −60 to −40 dBu). This signal travels via an XLR cable to a preamplifier (preamp), which boosts it to line level (approximately +4 dBu in professional settings). The amplified analogue signal then passes through an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC), which samples the signal at a set sample rate (e.g., 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz) and quantises each sample to a set bit depth (e.g., 24-bit). The resulting digital data stream is passed to the DAW via an audio interface, where it is written to disk as an audio file.
keyPoints: Microphone converts acoustic energy to a mic-level analogue electrical signal
Preamp boosts the signal to line level
ADC converts the analogue signal to digital (sample rate and bit depth)
Digital data passes to the DAW via audio interface
DAW records the data to disk as an audio file
questions.explanation: Understanding signal flow is essential for gain structure decisions. Gain is applied at the preamp stage — too little and the ADC noise floor becomes audible; too much and the ADC clips at 0 dBFS. The goal is to maximise signal level relative to the noise floor while leaving sufficient headroom. Each stage of the chain must be correctly matched to avoid signal degradation.
